domain: Historical Theology / Ecclesiastical Politics / Commitment Systems
topic_summary: Analysis of the Council of Nicaea (325 CE) Christological dispute centered on the term 'homoousios' (consubstantial). Pro-Nicene and Arian readings of Christ's relationship to the Father instantiate structurally different authority systems, victim sets, and mechanisms for enforcing orthodoxy within early Christianity.

key_entities: Nicene Creed (325 CE text, especially 'homoousios' term)
Pro-Nicene faction (Athanasius, Alexander of Alexandria, imperial backing)
Arian faction (Arius, Eusebius of Nicomedia, subordinationist Christology)
Episcopal networks (competing authority structures for doctrinal adjudication)
Laity and subordinate clergy (subjects of orthodoxy enforcement)
key_tensions: Consubstantial vs subordinate Christology (ontological status of Christ)
Imperial-backed hierarchical authority vs distributed episcopal networks (legitimacy grounding)

axes.structural_delta: Christ fully divine, same substance as Father; generates hierarchical ecclesiastical authority enforcing creedal orthodoxy
axes.primary_observable: Conciliar enforcement mechanisms; anathema declarations; imperial backing
axes.selection_reason: First reading selected; highest centrality; dominant reading with imperial enforcement

axes.structural_delta: Christ subordinate, created by Father; generates distributed episcopal authority and alternative theological legitimacy claims
axes.primary_observable: Counter-councils; alternative episcopal networks; theological treatises resisting homoousios
axes.selection_reason: Second reading selected; structurally distinct authority grounding and victim set

axes.structural_delta: Christ of similar but not identical substance; compromise position seeking to avoid subordinationism while resisting full consubstantiality
axes.primary_observable: Homoiousios terminology adoption; mid-4th century compromise councils
axes.selection_reason: Third reading selected; illuminates compromise space between axiom-contradictory positions

axes.structural_delta: Father and Son as modes of one divine being; rejects triadic ontology entirely
axes.selection_reason: Deferred: already condemned pre-Nicaea; marginal to homoousios dispute proper

deferred_axes.deferral_reason: Already condemned pre-Nicaea (Sabellius); marginal to the homoousios dispute's core axis

omegas.description: Without Constantine's convening power and enforcement, does the Pro-Nicene reading collapse to one episcopal network among many? Imperial backing may be load-bearing for its high ε.
Does 'homoousios' mean the same thing in Greek philosophical context vs Latin 'consubstantialis'? Translation may introduce hidden drift in the kernel itself.
All three readings treat laity as enforcement targets, not interpretive agents. Is this a shared extraction that the kernel structure itself obscures?
Does homoiousios reading collapse into Pro-Nicene after 381 CE (Constantinople I)? If so, the rope becomes a piton of failed resistance.
omegas.source: F03 (Hasty Generalization) - rope classification may be unstable

fracture_scan.notes: F03 detected: Semi-Arian reading classified as rope, but historical collapse into Pro-Nicene orthodoxy post-381 CE suggests potential piton reclassification. Generated omega_semi_arian_collapse to bound this uncertainty.

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The term 'homoousios' in the Nicene Creed as stabilized text defining Christ's ontological relationship to the Father
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Conciliar authority (episcopal consensus under imperial convening) claims interpretive legitimacy via apostolic succession and scriptural exegesis
commitment_system_recognition.candidate_pattern: Constitutional Ambiguity (homoousios term deliberately imprecise to secure consensus, enabling divergent readings)

readings.commitment: Christ is homoousios (consubstantial) with the Father - identical divine substance
readings.authority_grounding: Conciliar majority + imperial enforcement + Athanasian theological elaboration
readings.expected_structural_delta: Hierarchical ecclesiastical authority with high enforcement ε; anathema as exclusion mechanism; benefits imperial-church alignment

readings.commitment: Christ is created and subordinate - not of identical substance with the Father
readings.authority_grounding: Alternative episcopal networks + scriptural literalism (e.g., 'Father is greater than I')
readings.expected_structural_delta: Distributed authority among non-Nicene bishops; resistance to imperial enforcement; alternative theological legitimacy

readings.commitment: Christ is homoiousios (of similar substance) - compromise position
readings.authority_grounding: Moderate bishops seeking unity without full consubstantiality commitment
readings.expected_structural_delta: Coordination mechanism for avoiding schism; lower enforcement ε than Pro-Nicene; historically absorbed into Pro-Nicene post-381

axiom_contradictions.basis: Consubstantiality (same substance) and subordinationism (created, lesser substance) are mutually exclusive ontological claims; no coherent framework can hold both Christ as fully divine and identical in substance AND Christ as created and subordinate
